summary: Deploy Salesforce metadata intelligently with automatic wave generation
description: Analyzes your Salesforce metadata, generates deployment waves based on dependencies, and executes the deployment sequentially. This command orchestrates the entire smart deployment workflow.
examples: <%= config.bin %> <%= command.id %> --source-path force-app --target-org myorg --rollback-from v1.2.0 --rollback-to v1.2.1
flags.validate-only.summary: Validate the local wave plan without deploying
flags.source-path.summary: Path to the Salesforce project to analyze and deploy
flags.source-path.description: Defaults to the current working directory when omitted
flags.report-dir.summary: Directory for dry-run deployment plan reports
flags.report-dir.description: Defaults to .smart-deployment/reports/start-dry-run under the scanned project root
flags.allow-cycle-remediation.summary: Allow conservative cycle remediation for supported ApexClass cycles
flags.allow-cycle-remediation.descriptio: Applies temporary reversible source edits for simple cycles only
flags.use-ai.summary: Use AI for intelligent priority weighting and dependency inference
flags.use-ai.description: Enables provider-backed analysis for deployment prioritization
flags.org-type.summary: Organization type context for AI analysis
flags.industry.description: Provides business context to AI for better prioritization
flags.scope-commits.summary: Comma-separated commit SHAs or refs to include in the deployment scope
flags.scope-commits.description: Limits the deployment plan to metadata changed by these commits plus required dependencies.
flags.scope-manifest.summary: Path to a JSON commit or story scope manifest
flags.scope-manifest.description: Reads commits from { commits: [] } and { stories: [{ commits: [] }] } to scope validation and deployment planning.
flags.scope-manifest-output.summary: Write the resolved story scope manifest for CI review
flags.scope-manifest-output.description: Creates a deterministic JSON contract containing commits, changed files, included metadata, dependency-retained metadata, explicitly included metadata, and ignored metadata.
flags.destructive.summary: Delete metadata components using destructive wave manifests
flags.destructive.description: Runs the normal analysis path, then executes destructiveChanges manifests in reverse wave order.
flags.rollback-from.summary: Git ref or release tag that represents the rollback target state
flags.rollback-from.description: Use with --rollback-to. Modified or deleted metadata is restored from this ref using normal deploy waves.
flags.rollback-to.summary: Git ref or release tag that represents the release being rolled back
flags.rollback-to.description: Use with --rollback-from. Metadata added between refs is deleted using destructive waves.
